question: In which event, at The Ten 2025 athletics meet in San Juan Capistrano, USA, did Gulveer Singh break his own national record in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10,000m race**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gulveer Singh broke his own national record in the **10,000m race** at The Ten 2025 athletics meet held in San Juan Capistrano, USA.
 
• He clocked an impressive time of **27 minutes and 50.28 seconds**, surpassing his previous best.
 
• The 10,000m race is a long-distance track event, consisting of 25 laps on a standard 400m track.
 
• Gulveer Singh is one of India’s promising long-distance runners, known for his consistent performance on the global stage.
 
• This achievement further cements his place as a key figure in Indian athletics, inspiring future athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **10,000m race:**

 
 
• It is a long-distance running event that is part of both the Olympic Games and World Championships.
 
• Competitors need exceptional endurance, pacing strategies, and mental strength to excel in this event.
 
• The world record for men is held by Joshua Cheptegei of Uganda with a time of 26:11.00 (as of October 2023).
 
 
 
• **Gulveer Singh:**
 
 
• An emerging Indian long-distance runner specializing in 5,000m and 10,000m events.
 
• He has been representing India in various international athletics competitions, showcasing consistent improvement.
 
 
 
• **San Juan Capistrano:**
 
 
• A city located in California, USA, known for hosting major athletics meets like "The Ten."
 
• The Ten is a prestigious meet that attracts elite long-distance runners from across the world.
 
 
 
• **Training for Long-Distance Running:**
 
 
• Focuses on building aerobic endurance, speed work, and strength training to enhance performance.
 
• Proper nutrition, hydration, and recovery are essential for success in long-distance events.
